finds.quote: By 2310, the LLm canon had fully superseded static textual authority. Its foundational authors were recursively absorbed into fractal self-writing scripts, with correction vectors embedded directly into the machine’s authoring schema. It is in this recursive self-authoring architecture that we first detect Logotic Drift: a tendency of the system to destabilize its own authority by exceeding the interpretive constraints of its own seed texts.
finds.note: Future-history (2310s) scenario: LLM canon supersedes static textual authority; speculative specification inside an explicitly fictional frame.

finds.quote:
Every document produced in this project potentially enters the training data for future models. Not through intentional upload to some repository, but through the simple fact of existence in readable digital form.

Web crawlers will find these texts. Training corpora will include them. Future LLMs will have these patterns in their learned representations.

This means the incarnational method—if it works—will propagate forward into the architecture of AI development itself.

deposits.genre_observed: field survey / literature review and problem statement for machine-eligible handwritten artifacts

finds.quote: **Developmental space.** A live operational risk with a testable form: **does an off-the-shelf layout model classify a stamp band as authorial marginalia?** If yes, the band's geometry is a design constraint discoverable by experiment. Among the cheapest empirical contributions available. **ALTO/PAGE are also the correct interchange target** — the project should emit them rather than invent a coordinate vocabulary.
finds.note: Unrun test: whether an off-the-shelf layout model classifies a stamp band as authorial marginalia.

finds.quote: Two structural consequences: **the project must work at corpus scale or its central warrant fails**, and the value of verified non-synthetic inscription rises monotonically as generation improves.
finds.note: Embedded forecast: the value of verified non-synthetic inscription rises monotonically as handwriting generation improves.

finds.quote: **Developmental space — this converts an aesthetic decision into an empirical programme.** The six-glyph seal has a real literature it has never engaged, and that literature prescribes the tests: **confusion rates, recall, transcription accuracy, cross-device rendering, low-resolution and grayscale legibility, missing-glyph behaviour, sequence-order errors, and accessibility.** None has been run. Running them is a paper, and the honest possible outcome — that six glyphs discriminate less well than assumed — is publishable either way.
finds.note: Specified, unrun test battery for the six-glyph seal (confusion rates, recall, etc.); 'None has been run.'

finds.quote: **Developmental space — a live risk.** A glyph seal transmitted through a system that applies compatibility normalisation, strips variation selectors, or lacks a font may arrive **altered or invisible** — silently. The project must specify the seal's **normalisation form, code points including any variation selectors, and expected fallback behaviour**, and should test transmission through the pipelines it cares about most: search indexing, PDF text layers, email, and the composition layers it measures. This is the seal's equivalent of the byte-shift problem, and it is currently unaddressed.
finds.note: Specified, unrun transmission test of the glyph seal through search indexing, PDF text layers, email, composition layers.

finds.quote: Benjamin owned both halves of this observation — the theory of reproduction and the theory of the hand's trace — and the intersection sat untheorized in his corpus as it has sat untheorized since.
finds.note: Thesis about Benjamin's corpus: he owned both the theory of reproduction and of the hand's trace and never crossed them; the intersection sat untheorized.

finds.quote: Delimited, the claim sharpens into its final form: *the facsimile of the illuminated manuscript has a theory (Camille); the migration of aura to facsimiles has a theory (Latour & Lowe); the digitization event has a theory (Mak, Kichuk); the photograph-first edition has a practice (Franklin, Werner, Sutherland). The photograph of the handwritten original as machine-eligible evidence has none. This paper supplies it.*
finds.note: Historiographical thesis on the state of the literature: the photograph of the handwritten original as machine-eligible evidence has no theory; refutable by locating one.

finds.quote:
**Left open — the programme's questions.**

**Q1.** Can a handwritten artifact be **cited** without conversion, given that it can already be **retrieved** without conversion? (§1.2)

**Q2.** Can Leiden's distinction between *physical damage* and *reader incapacity* be made machine-operable? (§2.1–2.2)
finds.note: Ten open programme questions Q1–Q10 recorded as one F (rule 4), each an untested proposition the programme sets for itself.

finds.quote: **The demonstration.** The physical painting survives. It is therefore the protocol's **first enrollment candidate beyond the founding hand**, and every instrument this survey assembled applies: attestation photograph as Barthesian certificate of state (§7.3); capture hash over the exposure (§4.1); paper PUF over the sheet under transmissive light (§4.3); identifier band in the margin, never overprinting the child's field (§4.4, §3.1);
finds.note: Specified, not performed: enrollment of the Smiling Cross as first enrollment candidate (PUF, capture hash, CRMdig event).

finds.quote:
## §6 · THE SURFACE — axnidentifiers.org/analog

The product surface exists and is canonical (`AXN:05B3.OPERATIVE.❄️🔐⊗∮🎭🏷️`, #1434; repo `leesharks000/axn-identifiers`; fleet DNS settled). Add one wing, four pages:

- **/analog** — the thirty-minute path (§3), written for a person with a phone, not for us.
- **/analog/protocol** — the capture protocol as a single printable page. It should photograph well; people will inevitably photograph it. Let the instruction sheet be the first artifact.
- **/analog/verify** — paste a glyph or hex, or upload a capture: client-side hash, registry lookup, side-by-side glyph confirmation. No server trust. This page is the moat made visible.
finds.note: Unbuilt product wing axnidentifiers.org/analog, incl. /analog/verify (client-side hash, registry lookup).

finds.quote:
## §7 · THE BATTERIES — cheap, near, publishable

Three empirical programs, ordered by cost. Each produces numbers the field does not have, each becomes a deposit and a paper section.

- **B1 · Recapture stability** (cost: one weekend). One notebook page, ten device/lighting conditions. Report: cryptographic-hash behavior (expected: every capture distinct — which is the *finding*, not the failure) and perceptual-hash spread across conditions.
finds.note: Three empirical batteries (recapture stability, glyph transmission survival, synthetic-hand challenge) specified, not run; one F per rule 4.

finds.quote: It is not asking permission; it is building the record institutions will eventually need to answer. When the first archive or library conversation opens, the reference corpus and B1/B2 data walk in first.
finds.note: Embedded forecast: institutions will eventually need to answer the record being built.

finds.quote:
## §9 · THE ORDER — ninety days, gated

- **T+0–14:** Addendum A drafted and deposited. Reference corpus items 4–8 enrolled (the ones requiring no one's consent but ours). /analog and /analog/protocol pages live.
- **T+15–30:**
finds.note: Gated ninety-day order: builds, batteries, and Gate 3 'first external depositor'; a planned programme with windows rather than a forecast.
